summary: Video or audio stimulus with an overlay, timed capture and a controlled start. Covers a single-stimulus player and a multi-stimulus feed.
use_when: the request names a platform: "looks like a YouTube player", "like TikTok", "like Reels"
there is a video or audio stimulus and exposure must be measured
an external player SDK is involved
warnings: No template ships in this release. Scaffold from `basic`, then apply the spec_template below and this archetype's answers. `basic` is the reference structure.

Media is the highest-risk archetype here. Every version of the reference implementation lost time to one of: blocked autoplay, unscoped selectors colliding with the theme, inherited CSS that could not be overridden, or a version marker that drifted. Read reference/04-client-runtime.md before writing any of it.
Sound is a research-validity question, not a technical one. A respondent who watches an advertisement silently produces data that looks complete and is not.
An SDK bundle from a third party is an unapproved origin until it is in spec.json approved_origins with a reason.

questions.ask: One stimulus per question, or a feed of several? If a feed, how many, and is the order fixed, rotated, or randomised?
questions.why: A feed needs a manifest in row text, a rotation rule, and per-slot capture keyed to the item rather than the slot. A single stimulus needs none of that. Building the feed machinery for a single stimulus is the commonest overreach.
affects: whether a rotation rule is needed

questions.ask: Is sound required for the data to be valid?
questions.why: Browsers block unmuted autoplay without a user gesture, and a swallowed rejection is a frozen frame that is invisible in the export. If sound matters, the feed must open behind a tap-to-start gate. If it does not, muted autoplay is acceptable and the mute state must be captured per stimulus.

questions.ask: Which player or SDK, and which account? Is the player configuration something we control or something we inherit?
questions.why: Streaming behaviour, title chrome and rendition selection may live in a vendor player configuration you cannot see from the package. Knowing that up front stops you from trying to fix in code what belongs in configuration.
affects: what to ask the account owner

questions.ask: What must be measured per stimulus? Watched seconds, completion, interactions with timestamps, an ordered event log?
questions.why: This is the capture contract and it is unrecoverable once fieldwork starts. An ordered event log needs a capacity, a count and an overflow flag decided now.

questions.ask: Can the respondent skip, and can they go back?
questions.why: Skippability interacts with everything: navigation locks, whether an advertisement slot can be bypassed, and whether persisted state must survive a refresh.

questions.ask: Which devices, and is touch navigation required?
questions.why: Touch, autoplay policy and viewport behaviour cannot be validated by emulation. If touch matters, a real-device handoff is mandatory before acceptance.

questions.ask: Is a watermark or anti-piracy overlay required?
questions.why: It is a common ask and a common source of damage: the reference implementation's watermark styled hundreds of unrelated page elements and hid the wrong tiles, because it selected on theme class names without scoping.
affects: whether an overlay subsystem exists at all

parameters.name: start_gate
parameters.desc: 1 = show a tap-to-start panel and begin on the respondent's tap. Required for sound: browsers block video with audio until the respondent has interacted with the page. 0 = autoplay muted.

parameters.name: start_gate_text
parameters.desc: Caption on the start panel. To translate it, point this at a survey resource such as ${res.my_label}.

parameters.name: allow_skip
parameters.desc: 0 = the respondent must watch to the end before continuing. 1 = they may skip.

parameters.name: capture_watched
parameters.desc: Name of the survey variable holding seconds watched. Must match the pasted capture block.

parameters.name: capture_events
parameters.desc: Name of the survey variable holding the ordered event log. Must match the pasted capture block.

capture.label: __DQ_UPPER___WATCHED
capture.desc: Seconds of the stimulus actually watched, to two decimal places.

capture.label: __DQ_UPPER___EVENTS
capture.desc: Ordered event log, one event per row: sequence, elapsed ms, action, value.
capture.note: capacity is 60; the runtime also writes a count and an overflow flag so truncation is never silent

capture.label: __DQ_UPPER___EVENT_COUNT
capture.desc: How many events occurred, which may exceed the 60 rows recorded.
